title: Động vật hoang dã trong vườn thú · Agree / Disagree
prompt: Some people believe that phasing out zoos that primarily display animals for entertainment should be a priority. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

grammar.name: Động từ khuyết thiếu và mức độ khẳng định
grammar.example: Ending entertainment-led zoos could prevent future confinement, but animals already dependent on human care may suffer if closure arrives before suitable accommodation is secured.
grammar.why: Trong câu “Ending entertainment-led zoos could prevent future confinement, but animals already dependent on human care may suffer if closure arrives before suitable accommodation is secured.”, could điều chỉnh mức độ khẳng định hoặc nghĩa vụ, không tạo một bảo đảm tuyệt đối. Loài có nhu cầu xã hội và không gian phức tạp có thể căng thẳng trong nơi trưng bày. Dừng nhân giống chỉ để duy trì tiết mục tác động nguồn tạo thêm động vật bị giam.

grammar.name: Đối lập hai mệnh đề
grammar.example: Ending entertainment-led zoos could prevent future confinement, but animals already dependent on human care may suffer if closure arrives before suitable accommodation is secured.
grammar.why: Trong câu mở, but nối lợi ích dự kiến với giới hạn thực hiện cụ thể. Khung thời gian phân biệt cá thể chưa sinh với cá thể đang được chăm sóc; chính sự phân biệt này cho thấy dừng nhân giống và đóng cửa tức thì có hệ quả khác nhau.

paragraphs: Ending entertainment-led zoos could prevent future confinement, but animals already dependent on human care may suffer if closure arrives before suitable accommodation is secured. I support a funded phase-out of entertainment-led zoos, with lifetime care for existing animals and separate assessment of institutions doing credible conservation work.

Phasing out entertainment-led institutions can reduce unnecessary confinement. Complex species may experience chronic stress when their physical and social needs cannot be met. An institution could stop breeding animals merely to maintain a popular display. Stopping unnecessary breeding reduces the number of future animals dependent on restricted facilities, creating a gradual welfare route rather than an abrupt abandonment of present residents. Ending display-led breeding can prevent further confinement, but animals already dependent on human care may be unable to survive if simply released.

Closing facilities abruptly can leave existing animals without suitable long-term care. Existing captive animals may lack the skills, health or habitat needed for release, while sanctuaries have limited capacity. Abrupt closure can therefore remove current care before a suitable replacement exists, making a policy intended to reduce suffering create new welfare problems. Lifetime care plans and independent conservation criteria allow transition without confusing commercial display with credible species protection or assuming release is always humane. A closure timetable should follow funded care placements, with existing facilities maintaining responsibility until an independent assessment confirms that each transfer meets the animal’s needs. A phase-out should be judged by lifetime welfare and credible conservation outcomes, not by the number of facilities closed or animals described as returned to nature.
Success means fewer animals bred for display and secure care for those already captive; closure statistics alone cannot show that animal welfare has improved.
